model_and_data: The quoted experiments are modern deep-learning tasks, with three architecture families: ResNets, standard CNNs, and Transformers. ResNet18 uses layer widths [k, 2k, 4k, 8k], and the standard ResNet18 corresponds to k = 64. The quoted CNN family is a simple 5-layer CNN with 4 convolutional layers of widths [k, 2k, 4k, 8k] and a fully connected layer. Transformers are the 6-layer encoder-decoder, scaled by embedding dimension dmodel, with fully connected width dff = 4·dmodel. Quoted datasets include CIFAR-10 with 15% label noise for the ResNet figure, CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10 for the ResNet18 model-wise figure, and IWSLT‘14 German-to-English together with WMT‘14 English-to-French subsampled to 200K sentences in the Transformer caption. Label noise of probability p is quoted as the correct label with probability (1 −p) and a uniformly random incorrect label otherwise, sampled only once and not per epoch. The appendix quotes random Fourier features on Fashion MNIST, equivalent to a two-layer network whose randomly initialized first layer stays fixed.
loss: These quoted losses are not one loss. ResNets and CNNs are trained with cross-entropy loss, and the image-classification appendix says that unless stated otherwise the experiments use cross-entropy. The Transformer caption quotes label-smoothed cross-entropy, and test loss measured as per-token perplexity. The sample-wise Transformer slice quotes test loss as per-word perplexity. The body quote says the random Fourier features second layer is initialized with 0s and trained with MSE loss. The figure-caption quote says that second layer is trained using gradient flow. Both wordings are left as printed. The Belkin citation quoted here used ℓ2 loss for decision trees, random features, and 2-layer networks; that citation is not the loss of the ResNet and CNN runs.
varied_axis: The extract keeps three experimental axes separate, and it also names further factors. Model-wise: test error of models of increasing size, for a fixed large number of optimization steps. Figure 2’s horizontal line is quoted as model-wise double descent, varying model size while training for as long as possible. Epoch-wise: the vertical line in that figure, with test error undergoing double descent as train time increases; the epoch-wise section studies a fixed, large architecture over the course of training, and another quote keeps the model fixed and increases training time. Sample-wise: the number of train samples, for a fixed model and training procedure. The quoted Transformer slice is per-word perplexity against the number of train samples, with a regime where more samples hurt performance. A separate sentence says the interpolation threshold was changed by varying the number of model parameters, the length of training, the amount of label noise, and the number of train samples. Those four factors are not collapsed into one axis. Effective model complexity is quoted as the maximum number of samples on which the training procedure can achieve close to zero training error, and training time is quoted as increasing that complexity. A separate quote says they unify the above phenomena by defining a new complexity measure they call the effective model complexity and conjecture a generalized double descent with, and the line stops there. That sentence says “the above phenomena”; it is not used here to collapse model-wise, epoch-wise, and sample-wise variation into one axis. A further preliminary quote says double descent also holds as the amount of regularization varies for a fixed model.
held_fixed_axes: Held quantities are quoted per axis, not as one shared freeze. Model-wise quotes hold a fixed large number of optimization steps while model size changes. The ResNet/CNN optimizer quote gives Adam with learning-rate 0.0001 for 4K epochs; the SGD learning-rate display continues off that line and is not repaired. The Figure 2 ResNet quote uses CIFAR-10, 15% label noise, data-augmentation, and Adam for up to 4K epochs. Epoch-wise quotes hold the model fixed, including a fixed large architecture, while training time changes. Sample-wise quotes hold the model and training procedure fixed while the number of train samples changes. The image-classification appendix quotes no explicit weight decay or dropout unless explicitly stated. Within a quoted width sweep, the family is the stated ResNet18, 5-layer CNN, or 6-layer Transformer.
interpolation_definition: Interpolate is quoted as achieve (close to) zero training error. Effective model complexity of a training procedure T, with respect to distribution D and ϵ > 0, is quoted as EMCD,ϵ(T ) := max {n | ES∼Dn[ErrorS(T (S))] ≤ϵ}, where ErrorS(M) is the mean error of model M on train samples S. The hypothesis quote says there is no principled way to choose ϵ and that they currently heuristically use ϵ = 0.1, and it stops at “a formal specification for”. The next quoted line contains “sufficiently smaller” and “sufficiently larger”. The critically parameterized regime is quoted as EMCD,ϵ(T ) ≈ n, where a perturbation that increases effective complexity might decrease or increase test error. Hypothesis 1 is quoted as informal. The epoch-wise peak is quoted at models trained just long enough to reach ≈0 train error.
assumptions: The main hypothesis can be informally stated.
The quote says there is no principled way to choose ϵ and that the authors currently heuristically use ϵ = 0.1.
For ResNets and CNNs, the quote says training uses cross-entropy loss, with Adam at learning-rate 0.0001 for 4K epochs on that line.
Unless stated otherwise, the image-classification experiments use the cross-entropy loss.
Label noise of probability p trains on samples that have the correct label with probability (1 −p) and a uniformly random incorrect label otherwise.
That label noise is sampled only once and not per epoch.
No explicit regularization like weight decay or dropout was applied unless explicitly stated, in the quoted image-classification setup.
The random Fourier features first layer is randomly initialized and fixed throughout training.
The random Fourier features second layer is initialized with 0s and trained with MSE loss.
The main result is quoted as an experimental validation of Hypothesis 1.
result_type: Finite experiment. The extract says the main result is an experimental validation of Hypothesis 1 under a variety of settings, and that Hypothesis 1 is informal. No asymptotic theorem for these deep-network runs is stated in the quoted passages. An appendix quote says both the model- and sample-wise double-descent phenomena exist even in the setting of Random, and the line breaks there. A quoted figure in that appendix is Random Fourier Features on Fashion MNIST. The extract says that fully understanding the mechanisms behind model-wise double descent in deep neural networks remains an important open question.
transfer_limits: The quoted runs are ResNets, 5-layer CNNs, Transformers, and random Fourier features with a fixed first layer and an MSE-trained second layer. Decision trees, random features, and 2-layer neural networks with ℓ2 loss, on tasks including MNIST and CIFAR-10, are attributed to a demonstration by Belkin et al., not identified in that sentence as this paper’s runs. The image-classification loss quoted for this paper’s ResNets and CNNs is cross-entropy. The extract says fully understanding the mechanisms behind model-wise double descent in deep neural networks remains an open question. The extract does not locate gradient-boosted trees or an essay corpus. A learned first layer is outside the quoted random-feature appendix, which keeps the first layer fixed.
